title: Robotics lab program: zones, equipment, clearances and utilities
notes: Areas are net targets for a ~200 m2 room. Plan ~25% extra for circulation (36" accessible routes, ADA 403.5.1). The design agent drops 'could' items first when space runs out.
Equipment footprints and reaches are typical manufacturer figures; verify against the exact model before construction.
Numbers marked basis=standard come from the cited standard; basis=guideline are university EHS design guidelines; basis=practice are common practice.

robot_types.label: Collaborative arm, ~0.85 m reach (e.g. UR5e, Franka FR3)
robot_types.safeguarding: collaborative operation per risk assessment; pedestal or bench mount

robot_types.label: Industrial arm (non-collaborative)
robot_types.safeguarding: perimeter fence with interlocked gate; must be inside a safeguarded space

robot_types.label: Autonomous mobile robot (e.g. TurtleBot 4, MiR250)
robot_types.safeguarding: test in the arena; charging dock

robot_types.label: Quadruped (e.g. Unitree Go2, Boston Dynamics Spot)
Humanoid (e.g. Unitree G1, ~1.3 m tall)
robot_types.safeguarding: overhead gantry with fall-arrest tether in the arena

robot_types.label: Small indoor drones (e.g. Crazyflie, sub-250 g quadrotors)
robot_types.safeguarding: netted flight volume; no flight outside the net

zones.label: Entry, PPE and lockers
zones.placement: at the main entrance, so people put on PPE on the way in and take it off on the way out

equipment.label: PPE station (glasses, face shields, hearing protection, lab coats)

requirements.text: Locate PPE storage near the entrance so users don and doff on the way in and out.
Provide day-use and long-term lockers for personal belongings; especially important near machinery and robots.
Access control (badge/RFID) limiting entry to trained users.

zones.label: Collaborative arm cells
zones.placement: against a wall with overhead power drop; away from the main circulation spine

requirements.text: Select collaborative robots where humans and robots share space; industrial robots need more safety infrastructure and space.
A documented safeguarding and risk-reduction assessment by a qualified robot safety assessor/integrator, done during initial design.
Comply with ANSI/A3 R15 series and ISO 10218-2:2025, which defines safeguarded spaces that may change with the application.
Keep at least 500 mm between the robot's maximum space and walls, columns or furniture so a body cannot be crushed.
Every robot must be lockable in a zero-energy state (lockout/tagout).
Guards must also contain debris from end effectors and failed tooling.
Emergency stop reachable from a seated position: 15-48 in above floor with clear floor space.

zones.label: Fenced industrial arm cell
zones.placement: corner location with controlled access; fence gate interlocked

requirements.text: Industrial robots must be contained within a safeguarded space (perimeter fencing) to prevent contact with people.
Security fencing is the main difference between demonstration and full-size industrial robot labs.
Perimeter fence at least 1,400 mm high; lower guards need extra measures (light curtain or laser scanner).
For a ~1.6 m tall robot with the nearest hazard 600 mm from the fence, the fence should be at least 2,000 mm high.
Mesh opening sets the minimum fence-to-hazard distance (e.g. 20 mm slots need at least 120 mm).
Guards designed per ISO 14120; interlocked access gate with lockout so the cell cannot restart with a person inside.

zones.label: Netted test arena with motion capture (AMRs, quadrupeds, humanoid, drones)
zones.placement: largest clear rectangle in the room, away from benches; ceiling-mounted cameras need line of sight

requirements.text: About 12 OptiTrack-class cameras cover a ~6 x 6 m capture volume.
Netting, impact-resistant materials, protected cameras with direct line of sight, glare-free adjustable lighting and blackout capability.
Indoor netted flight volumes in university labs range from ~40 m2 x 4.5 m (UMD) to 10 x 10 x 4 m (UNSW); a 6 x 6 x 3 m cage suits sub-250 g drones.
Dedicated robot walking and flight testing labs are standard zones in modern robotics facilities.

zones.label: Electronics benches (ESD protected area)
zones.placement: quiet side of the room, away from fabrication noise and dust

equipment.label: Soldering station (HEPA + carbon fume extractor arm)

requirements.text: Handle sensitive parts only inside an ESD Protected Area with clearly identified boundaries.
All conductive items on a bench share one ground; dissipative work surface or mat.
Fume extraction for rosin-flux soldering, placed close to the work; extraction arms conductive and grounded.
Non-combustible tables and shelving where heat-generating equipment (soldering, hot wire) is used.
Localized fume extraction is required while soldering; a hard-ducted hood is best, otherwise a portable snorkel unit.
Portable fume extractors need both HEPA (particulate) and activated-carbon (flux vapor) stages; replace filters on schedule.
Position extraction so fumes are pulled away from, not through, the worker's breathing zone; prefer lead-free solder.
Incident: extended soldering on an open bench caused exposure; corrective action made local extraction mandatory.

zones.label: Fabrication: 3D printers, laser cutter, benchtop CNC, hand tools
zones.placement: controlled-access area near exhaust; segregated from areas that do not need PPE; noisy equipment isolated

requirements.text: Without enclosures: at least 4 ACH for one 3D printer, 6 ACH for several; no recirculation to offices/classrooms.
Or use noncombustible enclosures connected to exhaust or HEPA + carbon filtration.
Laser cutters only in well-ventilated spaces, typically at least 6 ACH; exterior exhaust preferred.
Fire-resistant waste containers (FM 6921 / UL 1315 / UL 242) near laser cutters.
Put high-hazard machines (CNC, laser cutters) where access can be controlled.
Separate PPE-required areas from areas that do not need PPE; isolate noisy equipment.
Lockout/tagout energy isolation for each machine.
No carpet; easily cleanable, slip-resistant floors where cutting fluids are used.

zones.label: Battery charging and storage
zones.placement: near an exit, away from flammable storage and egress paths; in view of occupied benches so charging is supervised

equipment.label: Vented fire-rated lithium battery cabinet (with charging)

requirements.text: Charge LiPo batteries only inside a fire-resistant container; store charged packs in a flammable-storage cabinet in a LiPo bag/box.
Dedicated vented fire-rated cabinet; packs not touching; dry, room temperature, away from heat.
Never charge unattended or overnight; dedicated charging rooms need smoke detection and 30-minute fire separation.
Store LiPo at 3.7-3.8 V per cell for storage longer than 14 days.
Fire and Emergency Services review of battery charging systems.

zones.label: Storage: parts, raw stock, finished work, chemicals
zones.placement: along walls; chemical cabinet away from battery cabinet and hot work

requirements.text: Lack of storage is the most common end-user regret; plan for raw materials, chemicals, finished products and PPE.
Separate cabinets per chemical class with secondary containment; no drain disposal.

zones.label: Hardware-in-the-loop / test benches
zones.placement: between the electronics zone and the arena

equipment.label: HIL test bench (motor dyno, power analyzer)

requirements.text: Electronics and software development labs sit alongside walking and flight test labs.

zones.label: Software / desk area
zones.placement: near windows or daylight; quiet side

zones.label: Robot maintenance and repair bay
zones.placement: between storage and the arena so robots roll straight in from testing; near spare parts and the battery cabinet

requirements.text: Dedicated zones for robot repair and assembly, testing, storage and charging are standard in legged-robot labs.
A maintenance / payload station with tools, replacement parts and modular payloads; separate robot storage stations when not in use.
Joint and gearbox servicing (lubrication) needs a cleanable bench and containment for oils.
Humanoid packs are large (Unitree H1: 15 Ah, 0.864 kWh) and some robots hot-swap packs, so keep swap stock in the battery cabinet next door.

equipment.label: Repair bench (ESD mat, vise, torque tools)

zones.label: Kitchenette (refrigerator, sink, dishwasher, microwave)
zones.placement: physically separated from lab hazards (no food in work areas), next to the break area and restroom plumbing

equipment.label: Kitchen counter with sink and dishwasher

requirements.text: Kitchen clearance: 40 in between opposing counters/appliances (60 in in U-shaped kitchens).
Sink counter 34 in max with knee clearance (or parallel approach).
Clear floor space at each appliance; refrigerator/freezer and microwave controls within reach ranges.

zones.label: Accessible single-user restroom
zones.placement: enclosed room off the break area; door swings must not block the 60 in turning space

requirements.text: 60 in turning space; water closet centerline 16-18 in from side wall; seat 17-19 in; grab bars 33-36 in high.
Lavatory rim 34 in max with knee clearance below.
Eyewash within 10 seconds' travel of every task that uses chemicals; hands-free after activation; signed.

zones.label: Dining / break area
zones.placement: next to the kitchenette, outside the PPE zone

requirements.text: Dining surfaces 28-34 in high with knee clearance; at least 5% of seating accessible.

building_services.text: Ceiling bus duct with movable disconnects for power drops; power and compressed air from the ceiling so robots can be reconfigured.
Wall and ceiling cord reels labeled with rated amps, instead of extension cords.
All equipment NRTL listed (UL/ETL); check imported 3D printers.
GFCI/AFCI receptacles evaluated, required near water (kitchenette, restroom, eyewash).
36 in (3 ft) clearance in front of electrical panels.
No carpet in work areas; slip-resistant, cleanable floors; non-upholstered furniture.
Acoustic review for compressors, CNC and dust collection; consider adjacent spaces.
Fire extinguisher type and placement reviewed by Fire and Emergency Services.
